methodology: Bounded first-pass verse screening. Compared narrative contours against known biblical passage locations, but primary editions/translation witnesses were not independently collated in this run. Every external reference is an unverified research lead, not a public association. Checked previous PR #276 and open security PR #93; no public promotion or database mutation.

records.topic: Command to enter the settlement humbly and ask forgiveness
records.notes: Qur'an depicts entry with a prescribed penitential formula; the biblical wilderness refusal and Jericho entry narratives do not give the same formula or identify the settlement here.
records.pending_question: Determine whether the 'gate' and ḥiṭṭa command have a distinctive pre-Islamic textual witness; avoid equating the unspecified town with Jericho as a verified fact.

records.topic: Wrongdoers substitute the commanded saying and incur punishment
records.notes: Biblical punishment episodes concern rebellion and plague, not the Qur'anic replacement of a commanded utterance; motif similarity is insufficient.
records.pending_question: Inspect Hebrew and Greek accounts and early Jewish exegesis for a precise altered-utterance tradition.

records.topic: Seaside town tested through Sabbath fish appearing
records.notes: Sabbath prohibition and commerce with fish occur in biblical tradition (Nehemiah), but no cited passage narrates fish appearing only on the Sabbath as a divine test.
records.pending_question: Verify Nehemiah's fish-market wording and assess dated Jewish Sabbath narratives without assuming the town's identity.

records.topic: Group questions admonition of Sabbath transgressors
records.notes: Duty to warn wrongdoers is a broad ethical motif; no specific pre-Islamic account of this three-group dialogue has been established.
records.pending_question: Review early Jewish commentary for a close dialogue, without turning general admonition texts into direct parallels.

records.topic: Warners saved and wrongdoers punished for defiance
records.notes: Collective judgment and distinction between righteous and guilty are broad biblical motifs; cited passages do not reproduce the Sabbath-fish story or its particular rescue.
records.pending_question: Check relation to Qur'an 7:166 and 2:65; inspect pre-Islamic Sabbath violation traditions and avoid inferring a specific punishment not stated in 7:165.
